correctness.rationale: Each n-gon width is exactly a shifted cosine arc of period 2q with q set by parity; integration proves Cq(r) and variance. Strict monotonicity follows from the monotone sinc function. A uniform Taylor expansion gives deterministic sup-norm O(q^2) coupling to a periodic quadratic random function and the covariance polynomial 1-15z²(2-z)²/8. The checker independently projects the vertices at nine polygon orders and five lags, finding maximum errors below 4e-9 for means and 3e-9 for covariances. Finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 25-page full open-access primary paper of Akiyama and Kamae (2022, arXiv:2201.06736v1) was examined. Theorem 1 supplies pairwise projected-edge expectations implying a finite lag-covariance computation; Theorems 3--4 already give equal width functions for suitable odd and double-even regular polygons. Both established facts are expressly excluded from novelty. The separate full uniform-in-angle normalized quadratic-process limit, its non-Gaussian law, and the strict angular anticorrelation with limiting value -7/8 are not established in that primary work. Actual result-record searches identified related one-point width and deterministic quadrature results but no equivalent stochastic-process limit; unindexed or inaccessible prior results remain possible. Although these new constants and the process limit are derivable with further analysis from the known cosine-arc representation, they require a separate angle-lag calculation and a functional-level uniform normalization not supplied as a statement or immediate numerical substitution in the source.
residual_risks: Akiyama--Kamae Theorems 1,3,4 already imply all finite-angle covariance computations via their edge kernel and the exact odd-to-double-even process pairing; these facts are not advanced as novel.
Accessible summaries of several indexed comparison records were not full-text inspections. A hidden implication in a related full paper cannot be categorically excluded.
Bibliographically unindexed equivalent limit-process calculations or generic Fourier limits may exist; targeted searches found none.

value.rationale: This supplies a complete process-level description of standardized random widths of polygons approaching a disk: convergence of the entire angular function under an explicit deterministic sup-norm coupling, a non-Gaussian limiting law and an exactly computable correlation polynomial with a sharp -7/8 anticorrelation minimum. It answers a natural joint-fluctuation question motivated by the 2022 width-deviation analysis, which records only scalar widths and moments. An earlier parity correspondence is only historical context, not a second independent contribution. No extrinsic downstream theorem is required for the structural value.
